scenarios.title_zh: CBSA 查验扣关：文件审阅或实物开箱导致放行慢
scenarios.title_en: Shipment held for a CBSA examination
scenarios.summary_zh: 货到港后被 CBSA 选中查验，柜子压在码头或查验场排队，客户催放行、担心仓储费与销售窗口。
customer_signals: Why is my shipment still flagged at customs?
CBSA 查验要多久？客户天天催我
Broker says it is an exam but gives no date — is something wrong with my invoice?
能不能加钱让它快点放行

empathy: 先承认客户的真实损失：销售窗口、仓储计时、他对下游的交期承诺，比「柜子还在海关」这件事更疼
不要说「这是 CBSA 的决定，我们也只能等」，这句话等于告诉客户没有人负责
判断客户此刻更怕坏消息还是没消息，多数是后者：先给节奏，再给结论
facts: CBSA 可对进口货物实施文件审阅、非侵入式（X 光/伽马）查验或实物开箱查验，属常规边境监管
被选中不等于申报有问题，也不等于必然补税或罚款，不要把「查验」和「有问题」画等号
把信息拆成「已核实」（柜在哪个场站、查验类型、是否已排期）与「待核实」（放行时间），对客户分开讲
plan: 让报关行确认查验类型与查验场地，记录查验通知编号，形成可复核的时间线
每 24 小时向查验场与报关行各催一次，记录对接人和回复内容
同步预备放行后的派送预约与文件，避免放行后再空等两三天
排队过长时评估同柜分票或更换查验场的可行性，并如实告知代价
sync: 承诺每天同一时间一条书面更新，含周末；「没有变化」也要发
状态从 held 变 released 的那一刻立即告知，不等下一个同步点
reassure: 明确这单由谁负责到底，给到客户联系人姓名与直线，而不是让他面对群聊
给可落地的替代方案：改派送地址、分批提货、给下游的英文延误说明

scripts.use_when: 客户第一次追问查验进度，情绪尚可控，但已有时限压力
scripts.text:
Hi {{customer_name}}, I can see why this is stressful — a hold at the border eats into a selling window you can't get back.

Here's what I've confirmed with our broker. Your shipment arrived at {{port}} and CBSA (Canada Border Services Agency) has selected it for examination. That is routine border control; it doesn't mean your declaration is wrong, and no penalty follows from being selected.

What we're doing: our broker has the exam request in and is chasing the terminal and the exam yard daily for a slot. I won't give you a release date I can't stand behind — exams finish when they finish, and I'd rather be straight than hand you a date and miss it.

I'll message you by {{next_update_time}} today with whatever the broker gives me, and the moment it flips to released.

scripts.use_when: 已回复过一次，客户再次追问；或当日无实质进展时主动同步
scripts.text:
Quick update on your shipment: still in the exam queue at {{port}}. Not what you wanted, so here's what actually moved today — our broker re-sent the exam request and got confirmation the container is on the yard list, and I've held a delivery slot for the day after release so we don't start from zero.

If it's still queued by {{next_update_time}} tomorrow, I'll ask whether another exam site clears faster and put the trade-off to you rather than just waiting.

scripts.use_when: 查验放行后说明结果，或客户情绪升级需要主管出面
scripts.text:
Hi {{customer_name}} — your shipment cleared the CBSA examination and was released this morning. No penalty was raised and nothing additional was assessed at release; the entry stands as filed.

Delivery is booked for {{delivery_date}}; I'll send the driver's details the day before. I'm sorry this one sat as long as it did. The exam yard was backed up, and I should have pushed for a site change a day earlier than I did.

Nothing further is needed from you. If your buyer wants confirmation, I'll send the release document. And I'm staying on this until it's signed for.

alts.text:
Hi {{customer_name}}, I'm sorry — I know this hold is landing right on top of commitments you've already made, and the storage clock makes it worse every day.

I've been through it with our broker. Your shipment is at {{port}} and CBSA has picked it for examination. That's a standard border check, not a finding against your shipment, and there's no penalty attached to it.

Our broker is pushing the exam yard for a slot every day, and I'll have a straight answer on the exam type for you by {{next_update_time}}. I'll write at that time regardless — even if the answer is that we're still in the queue.

If you need something in writing for your buyer, tell me and I'll put it together today.

Hi {{customer_name}} — status on your shipment: arrived at {{port}} and selected by CBSA for examination.

What that means: a routine border check. It isn't a ruling against your invoice, and no penalty follows from being selected. What I can't give you is a release date — exams move at the agency's pace, not ours.

What I'm doing: broker is chasing the exam yard daily, and I'm holding a delivery slot for the day after release.

I'll confirm the exam type by {{next_update_time}}, then update you daily until it's released. If the queue turns out long, I'll ask our broker whether another site clears faster and tell you what that costs in time.

common_causes: CBSA 风险布控或随机抽查（贸易合规、原产地、估价疑点）
发票与实物不符：品名笼统、数量对不上、型号缺失
同柜其他货主货物触发查验，整柜被连带查验
木包装无 ISPM 15 标识或残留树皮、土壤
HS 归类或原产地声明需要进一步核实
resolution_path: 向报关行确认查验类型（文件审阅 / 非侵入式 / 实物开箱）与查验场地
记录查验通知编号与预约信息，建立可复核的时间线
每 24 小时向查验场与报关行各催一次，留痕
评估同柜分票部分放行或更换查验场的可行性
查验完成并放行后，当日提交派送预约
如产生堆存，先按费用口径判定归属，再对客说明
internal.sla_hint: 首次响应 2 小时内；查验期间每 24 小时主动同步一次（含周末）；放行后 24 小时内给出派送计划；客户情绪升级时 4 小时内主管介入
internal.fee_policy: DDP 项下 CBSA 常规查验产生的查验与操作费用由我方承担，不向客户转嫁；因客户资料错误、地址错误或拒收导致滞箱、堆存、改址的，凭码头或船司单据书面列明后另行协商，未经确认不收费
guardrails: 不承诺放行日期，只给已排队/待排状态与条件，不用「大概几天」当承诺
不说查验是 CBSA 故意卡货，不评价执法，也不暗示有内部关系能提速
不建议改品名、改 HS、拆票或重做发票来降低下次被查概率

scenarios.title_zh: CARM 强制化与 RPP 担保未就位导致无法先放行
scenarios.title_en: Release blocked — CARM security not in place
scenarios.summary_zh: CARM 成为唯一记账系统后，进口商必须自备财务担保才能先放行后缴税；客户没有 BN、RM 账户或担保未上，货到港却只能先缴税，产生排队与堆存。
customer_signals: Broker says we need a bond before release — what is RPP?
为什么别的货代不用我注册 CARM，你们要？
我们有 BN 了，为什么还是不放行
能不能先用你们自己的保证金给我的货

empathy: 承认这套制度对中小进口商的冲击：多数人是第一次遇到「必须自己上担保」
说明这不是我方额外加码，而是过渡期结束后 CBSA 的统一要求，先把制度讲清楚再谈钱
避免让客户觉得被「要钱」，先解释它买到的是「先放行、后缴税」的时间
facts: CARM 自 2024-10-21 起是 CBSA 商业货物记账的系统，进口商不再能借用报关行的担保
RPP 需要进口商用自己的 BN 在 CARM Client Portal 注册 RM 账户并提交财务担保（现金押金或电子担保函）
报关行须先取得进口商在 CARM 门户的授权才能代为申报，未授权是最常见的卡关原因
未完成 RPP 的只能在放行时缴税（线下流程更慢）；担保额度按近 12 个月最高月度应收含 GST 计算，不足同样被拦
plan: 先确认本票谁是进口商（IOR）：DDP 下通常是我方，客户无需注册
若客户自任 IOR：发 BN→RM→RPP→担保四步清单与官方链接，给所需资料模板
核对我们的担保额度是否覆盖本票税额，不足则补足或走现金缴税
同时给「先缴税放行」的 B 方案与成本对比，让客户自己选
sync: 承诺当日给出一页纸的 A/B 路径对比，次日几点前确认
担保或注册类事项按工作日节奏更新，不承诺 CBSA 处理时长
reassure: 明确即使客户来不及注册，也能先提货，不让他因为制度问题丢销售窗口
把 CARM 问询前移到订舱环节，下次不会再临门一脚才发现

scripts.use_when: 客户第一次遇到 CARM/RPP 要求，质疑为何要自己注册或交保证金；发送前先确认本票 IOR 归属
scripts.text:
Hi {{customer_name}}, I understand why this feels like a wall out of nowhere — you booked a delivered price, and now there's a registration step you've never heard of.

Honest picture. Since CARM (CBSA Assessment and Revenue Management) became CBSA's system of record, an importer can get release before paying duties and taxes only if it holds its own financial security under the Release Prior to Payment program. The transition that let brokers cover it ended on 20 May 2025, so it applies to everyone, not just you.

The good news: we're checking which importer account this entry sits under. If it's ours, {{bill_no}} moves on our financial security and you need to register nothing; if it's your BN, I'll send the two steps and file with you.

I'll confirm in writing by {{next_update_time}} which route {{bill_no}} is on. Nothing is stuck while we sort this.

scripts.use_when: 已解释过制度，客户仍在犹豫是否自己注册，或等待担保确认
scripts.text:
Update on {{bill_no}}: I'm confirming which importer account the entry sits under — if it's ours, no registration is needed from you; if it's yours, I'll send the two steps.

If you want your own import account later, the order is Business Number from the CRA, then an RM account (a 6-character program number such as RM0001) in the CARM Client Portal, then financial security. It's a few steps, not a few weeks, but I won't quote you a CBSA turnaround.

I'll send the written confirmation by {{next_update_time}}.

scripts.use_when: 放行完成，同时把长期方案与这次沟通缺口一次说清
scripts.text:
Hi {{customer_name}} — {{bill_no}} was released this morning under our security, and delivery is booked for {{delivery_date}}.

To close the loop: you don't need a CARM account as long as the entry is filed under our importer account. If it turns out to be under your BN, I'll send the two steps and file with you.

I'm sorry this landed as a surprise at the worst moment. The RPP change should have been on your booking confirmation from the start, and it is now.

alts.text:
Hi {{customer_name}}, I'm sorry — this is exactly the kind of thing that shouldn't land on you at the last minute. You paid for a delivered service and now there's a registration question in the way.

Short version: under CARM (CBSA Assessment and Revenue Management), releasing goods before duties and taxes requires the importer to post its own financial security. Brokers can no longer lend theirs; that ended on 20 May 2025. It's a system change, not a problem with your company.

I'm confirming which importer account this entry sits under: if it's ours, {{bill_no}} clears on our security and you do nothing; if it's yours, I'll send the two steps.

I'll confirm the route in writing by {{next_update_time}}. You won't be left guessing.

Hi {{customer_name}} — quick answer on the CARM (CBSA Assessment and Revenue Management) request you received.

Why it came up: to release goods before duties and taxes are paid, the importer has to hold its own financial security under Release Prior to Payment. Broker security no longer covers it; that ended 20 May 2025.

What applies to you: I'm confirming which importer account this entry sits under. If it's ours, {{bill_no}} clears under our security and you do nothing; if it's yours, I'll send the two steps.

If you want your own import account later — useful for claiming GST input tax credits — say so and I'll send the Business Number, RM account and security steps.

I'll confirm {{bill_no}}'s release route in writing by {{next_update_time}}.

common_causes: 进口商未注册 BN 或 RM 账户，CARM 无法生成有效放行
进口商未提交财务担保（现金押金或电子担保函），不符合 RPP 资格
报关行未取得进口商在 CARM 门户的申报授权（BAM/PAM），无法代为提交 CAD
过渡期结束后仍沿用报关行担保：延长后的过渡期于 2025-05-20 03:00 EDT 结束（原定 2025-04-19），此后须自有担保
担保额度不足（按近 12 个月最高月度应收含 GST 计算）被系统拦截
收货公司 BN 变更、合并，CARM 账户资料与发票买方不一致
客户坚持自任进口商，但无加拿大税务注册
resolution_path: 确认本票进口商归属（我方 / 客户 / 第三方）并书面留档，话术口径与报关单据保持一致
确认报关行已在 CARM 门户取得进口商授权（BAM/PAM），以及本票的 CAD 提交权限
我方为 IOR：核对担保额度是否覆盖本票税额，不足则补足或先缴税
客户为 IOR：发 BN→RM→RPP→担保四步清单、官方链接与资料模板
给「先缴税放行」B 方案（在 CBSA 办公室缴税，信用卡上限 5,000 加元，或借记卡、支票）与时间成本对比
担保到位后 24 小时内重新提交，跟踪 CARM Client Portal 状态
结案复盘：把 CARM 问询写入订舱确认书，前置拦截
internal.sla_hint: 首次响应 2 小时内；CARM 与担保问题当日内给出 A/B 书面路径；每 24 小时同步一次；收到客户资料后 1 个工作日内提交
internal.fee_policy: DDP 项下我方作为进口商时，RPP 担保成本由我方承担，不向客户转嫁；客户自任进口商时，其担保或押金成本自付；因客户迟延提供 BN 或 RM 资料产生的滞港与堆存，凭实际单据书面列明后协商；我方垫付税金的，按约定账期回收，不计利息（另有约定除外）
guardrails: 发送话术前必须确认本票的进口商归属：若申报使用客户 BN，话术里不得说「以我方进口商账户申报」，须改走客户 CARM 注册路径
不替客户安排借用他人 BN 或共用进口商账户，也不建议这样做；不承诺 CARM 注册或担保审批所需天数
不把制度变化包装成我方新增收费，也不暗示可以绕过 RPP

scenarios.title_zh: 关税与 GST/HST 争议：DDP 已含税却又收到税单
scenarios.title_en: Duty and tax charge on a DDP shipment
scenarios.summary_zh: 客户认为 DDP 已含税，却收到 CBSA 或末端代收的税单，或质疑税率高于预期，要求退款或降税。
customer_signals: I already paid duty — why is there another tax bill?
DDP 不是包税吗，为什么还要我付 GST
My accountant says duty should be zero under a trade deal — why is it not?
为什么这批多收了 25%？之前从没有过

empathy: 先承认「以为包税却又被收钱」的观感很差，不要一上来讲法条
区分客户是「被重复收」还是「对税率有疑问」，这是两条不同的处理路径
客户提低报时先不评判，但要明确我方不会做，并把风险讲清楚
facts: DDP 含的是按申报价值与归类计算的关税、联邦 GST 5%，以及按进口省份适用税率的省税（PST/HST），各省不同
GST/HST 注册企业通常可作进项税抵扣，这部分未必是净成本
重复税单常见于末端或平台二次代收，也可能是预估与实评不同；归类或原产地差异同样改变税率，须按 CBSA 程序处理
2025–2026 年加拿大对含中国熔炼浇铸钢或冶炼铸造铝的货物、以及钢铁衍生品加征附加税，清单与税率以财政部最新公告为准；附加税按全额货值或清单税率叠加，不是 GST 算错
plan: 调取报关记录与 CBSA 评税明细，逐项列出完税价格、HS、税率、GST/HST、省税
与客户收到的账单逐笔比对，标出重复项与差异项
重复收费向收费方发起争议，取得书面撤销或退款确认
归类或估价争议走复议或自愿披露路径，先内部合规复核，不擅自改单
sync: 承诺给出「税单拆解表」的具体时点，而不是口头解释
涉及 CBSA 复议的按月给节点，不让客户干等
reassure: 明确能退的怎么退、多久退，不能退的用文件说明为什么
提供未来订单的税前预估模板，下次不再为同一件事争吵

scripts.use_when: 客户第一次质疑税单，或提出降税诉求；发送前先确认报价单是否含税
scripts.text:
Hi {{customer_name}}, I understand the frustration — you paid a delivered price, and a tax bill on top looks like being charged twice. Let me show you what's in it, not argue about the rate.

On a DDP shipment we cover duty, 5% federal GST and the provincial tax of the importing province, unless the quote expressly excludes them. Rates differ by province: a shipment into Alberta and one into Ontario don't carry the same tax. What we can't absorb is a second charge on the same goods from elsewhere in the chain; that we dispute, not pass on.

I've asked our brokerage for the CBSA assessment and entry summary to put beside your bill. You'll have it by {{next_update_time}}, line by line, with the classification used.

If it's an overlap, that's ours to correct. If the rate is simply higher than you expected, you'll see why.

scripts.use_when: 已完成比对，发现重复收费或需要客户接受税率依据；发送前先确认报价单是否含税
scripts.text:
The entry is back. Duty was assessed on the value we declared, plus 5% GST and the provincial tax for the importing province — I've put each line next to your invoice. A 25% line, if present, is the steel/aluminium surtax; I'll verify the list and the melt-and-pour declaration.

One line looks duplicated: the same GST appears on our invoice and on the carrier's collection. I'm raising it with the carrier today and will have their position by {{next_update_time}}.

Nothing needed from you until then.

scripts.use_when: 重复收费确认并退，或税率解释完成、客户接受结论；发送前先确认报价单是否含税
scripts.text:
Hi {{customer_name}} — the duplicate GST has been confirmed as a carrier collection error. It's being reversed, and the credit will show on your account; I'll send the confirmation document the moment it's issued.

The rest checks out: duty at the rate for the classification used, 5% GST, and the provincial tax for the importing province. The entry summary is attached so your accountant can see the basis.

I'm sorry you had to spend time on this. For your next order I'll send a tax estimate before booking. And if your company is GST-registered, ask about input tax credits on that portion — it often nets out.

alts.text:
Hi {{customer_name}}, I'm sorry — paying for a delivered price and then getting another tax bill feels like being taken for a ride. I'd be annoyed too.

What I can tell you straight away: our DDP price covers duty, the 5% federal GST and the provincial tax for the importing province. Those are the only taxes we should bill you for. A second charge usually comes from elsewhere in the chain, and that's worth chasing, not arguing about the rate.

I've asked our brokerage for the CBSA assessment and entry summary so I can lay both bills side by side. You'll have it by {{next_update_time}}, with each line explained.

If we've double-billed, that's mine to fix. If the figures are right, you'll at least see why.

Hi {{customer_name}} — on the extra tax bill, here's where it stands.

What DDP includes: duty, 5% GST, and the provincial tax for the importing province. Nothing else should reach you.

What I'm checking: the CBSA assessment against the invoice you received, line by line. Duplicate GST from a carrier collection is the usual culprit; a classification or valuation difference is the other one.

You'll have the breakdown by {{next_update_time}}. If there's an overlap, it's corrected at our end. I won't lower the declared value or change the classification to shrink a tax bill — that would put your goods and your company at risk, and I'm not going to do it.

common_causes: 客户对 DDP 覆盖范围理解偏差，以为只含运费
末端、平台或仓储方对同一票货二次代收 GST/HST
报关行按预估税额开票，CBSA 实际评税不同
归类或原产地判断差异导致关税高于客户预期
省税按进口省份（清关地）计，客户按收货地或供应商所在地估算
货物含钢铝成分或属钢衍生品，适用 2025–2026 附加税，客户误认为重复征税或算错
客户非 GST 注册主体，无法抵扣而把税视为纯成本
resolution_path: 调取报关记录、CBSA 评税与调整单据
逐项拆解：完税价格、HS、关税税率、GST/HST、省税、附加税
核查是否落入钢铝或钢衍生品附加税清单，索取供应商熔炼浇铸地声明与材质证明
与客户账单逐笔比对，标注重复项与差异项
重复收费：向收费方发起争议并取得书面撤销或退款确认
归类或估价争议：内部合规复核后评估复议或自愿披露路径

scripts.use_when: 客户第一次被告知资料不全，情绪尚好但已开始焦躁
scripts.text:
Hi {{customer_name}}, I know this is the third round on paperwork, and that's on us for not sending one clean list at the start. Let's fix it in a single pass.

For a Canadian entry the commercial invoice has to carry the seller and buyer names and addresses, the invoice number and date, a description specific enough to classify, quantity, unit and total value, currency, delivery terms, country of origin and tariff classification. The packing list then has to match it — cartons, gross and net weight, cube. When any of that is missing the entry can't be transmitted, and your shipment sits at {{port}}.

I'll send you a fill-in template in the next ten minutes. Whatever your supplier can complete, send back; I'll turn it into what our broker needs and return it for your sign-off.

I'll confirm transmission by {{next_update_time}}.

scripts.use_when: 模板已发，等待客户回料，或无进展时主动同步
scripts.text:
Template should be with you. The two fields suppliers usually can't answer are origin and classification — send me the product details and I'll take a first pass for you to confirm.

Nothing moved on your shipment today; it's still waiting on documents at {{port}}. If I have the invoice and packing list by tomorrow morning, our broker can still make the next window.

I'll check in by {{next_update_time}} either way.

scripts.use_when: 资料补齐并提交，说明后续与流程改进
scripts.text:
Hi {{customer_name}} — documents are in and the entry has been transmitted. Your shipment is with CBSA for release, and I'll tell you as soon as it comes through.

The template is yours to keep. If your supplier uses it from the first order, we won't repeat this. I should have sent it when you booked rather than after the goods landed — that's a gap in our process, not in yours.

I'll confirm release and start the delivery booking the same day. Nothing else needed from you for now.

alts.text:
Hi {{customer_name}}, sorry — you've been going back and forth on paperwork for days and that's our fault for not giving you one clear list on day one.

What CBSA needs on a commercial invoice: both parties' names and addresses, invoice number and date, a proper description, quantity, unit and total value, currency, delivery terms, country of origin and classification. The packing list has to agree with it exactly — cartons, gross and net weight, cube.

I'm sending a template you can hand straight to your supplier. Send it back in whatever state it's in, even half-filled, and I'll do the assembly and return it for a final look.

Meanwhile your shipment is sitting at {{port}} on documents, not on duty. I'll confirm where we are by {{next_update_time}}.

Hi {{customer_name}} — the short version of what's blocking your shipment at {{port}}: the invoice is missing the country of origin and the classification, and the packing list doesn't match the carton count.

Both are fixable today. I'm sending a template; your supplier fills what it can, you send it back, I convert it into the broker's format.

If I have it back by tomorrow morning we make the next transmission window. The one thing I can't do is invent the origin or the classification for you — that has to come from the supplier.

I'll confirm by {{next_update_time}} whether the entry has gone in.

scenarios.summary_zh: 到港后码头堆场满、铁路车皮不足，柜子提不出来或内陆点到不了；ETA 反复，客户下游排产受影响。

船到温哥华一周了还提不出来，是不是丢了
Rail is stuck again and my Toronto delivery date is gone
能不能改卡车，我加钱

empathy: 承认客户真正的损失在「下游承诺」而不是柜子本身：他要去跟自己的客户解释
不要把港口拥堵当成免责挡箭牌，客户买的是确定性，不是解释

scripts.use_when: 客户发现船已到港但柜子未提，开始担心丢件或错过交期
scripts.text:
Hi {{customer_name}}, I know this one hurts more downstream than it does at the port — you've made commitments to your own customers on the date we gave you.

Here's where it actually stands. Your shipment is discharged at {{port}}, but the terminal is working through a backlog and rail hasn't lifted it yet. That's the honest bottleneck. Nothing has happened to the cargo, and it isn't sitting somewhere unaccounted for.

There are two ways forward. We leave it on rail, which costs you time but no extra freight, or we pull it by truck, which cuts days off and adds cost. I'll have a firm truck number for you by {{next_update_time}} so you can decide rather than guess.

I'll send a status every day at the same time until it's moving, including the days when nothing has changed.

scripts.use_when: 延误持续，需要给客户一个明确的切换建议而不是继续等
scripts.text:
No change at {{port}} today — still waiting on a rail lift. What I did: escalated with the terminal's customer desk for on-dock rail priority, and got a trucking rate for the alternative.

If rail hasn't lifted your shipment by tomorrow, my recommendation is to switch and stop burning calendar days. Your call, and I'll hold the truck quote for 48 hours.

Next update by {{next_update_time}}.

scripts.use_when: 柜子已提出并上铁路，或已切换卡车、货物恢复流动
scripts.text:
Hi {{customer_name}} — your shipment has been lifted and is moving inland. Rail picked it up this morning, and the ramp schedule puts it in your city later this week.

I'm sorry about the gap between the arrival date we gave you and what actually happened. The terminal backlog wasn't in our control; telling you two days sooner that the rail lift was slipping was, and I didn't.

Delivery is booked for {{delivery_date}}, and I'll confirm the appointment as soon as the container is grounded. If a short delay letter to your customers would help, say the word.

alts.text:
Hi {{customer_name}}, I'm sorry — I know a slip at the port lands on commitments you've made to other people, and that's the part that actually costs you.

What I can confirm: your shipment is off the vessel at {{port}} and sitting on the terminal, waiting for a rail lift. The terminal is behind and rail capacity is tight, which is why the date moved. The cargo is fine, and nothing is missing.

I'm pushing for an on-dock rail slot and getting a trucking price in parallel, so you'll have a real choice rather than a wait.

I'll write to you by {{next_update_time}} with the truck number and whatever rail tells us. After that, a message every day until it's moving — including the days when there's no news.

Hi {{customer_name}} — where your shipment stands: discharged at {{port}}, still on the terminal, no rail lift yet. That's the delay, and it's a capacity problem at the terminal and on rail, not a problem with your cargo.

Two options: stay on rail, no extra freight, more days; or switch to truck, faster, extra cost.

I'll have the truck price by {{next_update_time}} and a rail position at the same time. If rail hasn't lifted by then, I'd suggest we switch.

Daily update from me until it moves.

customer_signals: Why am I being charged storage when the delay wasn't mine?
这笔堆存费凭什么我出
Can you get the terminal to waive it?
I never agreed to these charges

empathy: 先承认「不是我的错却要我付钱」的不公平感，这比金额本身更伤关系
在谈钱之前先把时间线摆出来，让客户看到每一段是谁造成的

scripts.use_when: 客户第一次收到堆存账单并提出异议
scripts.text:
Hi {{customer_name}}, I'd push back too if a bill landed for days I didn't cause. So before we talk about who pays, let me show you the timeline.

Your shipment arrived at {{port}} on {{eta_date}}, and I have the CBSA release timestamp. The terminal's free storage ran out partway through that gap, and the charges start from there. Some of that gap is terminal backlog, some is the examination, and some is time we spent waiting on documents. Those three are not the same thing, and they shouldn't all land on you.

I'm building the breakdown now: terminal in and out dates, the last free day, and the release timestamp. You'll have it by {{next_update_time}}, split by cause.

The part that's ours, we carry. The part that's documented on your side, I'll show you the tariff line. Nothing gets deducted before you've seen the numbers.

scripts.use_when: 责任分段已完成，需要把结论与下一步摆清
scripts.text:
Breakdown is with you now. The statement splits the charge by cause: the terminal backlog and the examination fall before release, and the days after release are the part I'd like to discuss with you rather than just bill.

I've filed a waiver request with the terminal on the pre-release portion and will chase it weekly.

The post-release days I'd like to talk through with you before they go on an invoice. Can we speak tomorrow?

scripts.use_when: waiver 有结果、双方就分担达成一致后
scripts.text:
Hi {{customer_name}} — the terminal credited the pre-release days we disputed, so those charges are gone. The remaining {{amount}} stands for the days after release, and I've split them across your next two invoices as we agreed.

Thank you for working through the timeline with me instead of refusing the bill. It made the waiver case much easier to argue.

Two changes on our side: I'm booking the delivery appointment before release rather than after, and I'll flag the free-time expiry date the moment a container is discharged, so this doesn't surprise either of us again.

alts.text:
Hi {{customer_name}}, I'm sorry — a storage bill for days you didn't cause is genuinely unfair, and I don't want to hand you a number and walk away.

Here's what I'm doing. Your shipment arrived at {{port}} on {{eta_date}}, and I've pulled the terminal's in and out dates, the last free day, and the exact time CBSA released it. That splits the charge into what was the terminal and the examination, what was our own slow paperwork, and what fell after release.

The first two are ours. I'll carry them and ask the terminal to waive them, because it's worth asking.

You'll have the split by {{next_update_time}} with the tariff lines quoted. If any part is properly yours, we'll agree it together before anything is invoiced.

Hi {{customer_name}} — on the storage charge: I'm not asking you to accept it as it stands.

Your shipment arrived at {{port}} on {{eta_date}}, so I'm pulling the terminal in and out dates, the last free day, and the CBSA release time to split the charge by cause. Terminal backlog and the examination are ours. Post-release delays get looked at separately.

You'll have the split with tariff references by {{next_update_time}}. I'll also file a terminal waiver for the portion we're absorbing — no promises on the outcome, but it's worth the ask.

Nothing is invoiced until you've seen the numbers.

scripts.text:
Hi {{customer_name}}, that's a bad way to receive a shipment, and if you've promised these units to someone, it's worse.

I've seen the photos you sent. Before I speculate about cause, I need the full set, because it's harder to gather later: all six sides of the damaged cartons, the pallet label, any note the driver wrote on the proof of delivery, and a video of the unpacking if the contents are still inside. That's what a surveyor will ask for.

What happens next: I'll appoint an independent surveyor within 48 hours, and open the carrier claim in parallel rather than waiting for the survey.

Once you have a repair or replacement quote, send it through.

I'll come back to you by {{next_update_time}} with the surveyor's booking and an honest view of timing. I won't say it'll be quick; I'd rather be accurate.

In parallel I've filed the carrier claim and asked the co-loader whether other consignments in the same container came through wet, since that answer shapes the cause.

Nothing needed from you today. I'll send the survey summary the day I get it, and I'll chase weekly in between.

scripts.use_when: 验货报告出具，索赔已提交，需要管理客户预期

The claim is now with the carrier, and I've sent you the report plus the claim reference. On recovery I'll be straight with you: the limit under the bill of lading is rarely the full value, so the settlement may not cover the whole loss. You'll get the number as soon as it's offered, not before.

In the meantime the replacement units are quoted, and I can hold that price for a week.

I'm sorry this landed on you.

With that I'll appoint a surveyor and file against the carrier at the same time, rather than waiting for one to finish before starting the other.

I'll be back to you by {{next_update_time}} with the survey date and a claim reference.

scripts.use_when: 客户第一次报告少箱或短少，通常很急
scripts.text:
Hi {{customer_name}}, a missing carton is rarely just a carton — if it's the one part your customer needs, the whole order is late. Let me find out where it went.

Three records will tell us: the loading list and container photos from origin, the tally sheet from the freight station where the container was devanned, and the delivery receipt. Where they disagree tells us whether this was short-shipped at origin or lost on the last leg, and the fix is different for each.

While I pull them, send me your count by carton number and model, plus photos of what actually arrived on the dock. Don't move the pallet yet.

I'll have the comparison by {{next_update_time}} and I'll tell you which of the two it looks like. If it's short-shipped, your supplier needs to know today, not next week.

scripts.use_when: 比对已开始，需要让客户知道我们在查哪里
scripts.text:
Tally from the freight station shows every carton was received into the CFS, which points away from short shipment and towards the last leg.

I've asked the delivery depot for the driver's return sheet and for any over-goods sitting in their warehouse — a stray carton turns up there more often than you'd think.

Comparison summary by {{next_update_time}}. If it doesn't surface by then, I'll open a claim the same day rather than keep looking.

scripts.use_when: 找到箱并安排补派，或确认丢失进入索赔
scripts.text:
Hi {{customer_name}} — the carton was in the depot's over-goods rack. It had been scanned onto the wrong route that day and has been sitting there since. It goes out to you tomorrow on the same run.

I'm sorry you spent a week chasing it. The tally sheet was there from the start and I should have pulled it on day one instead of asking you to recount.

I've asked the depot to photograph every over-goods item at close of day, so this gets caught in hours rather than days. Next shipment, I'll send you the tally before the truck leaves.

alts.text:
Hi {{customer_name}}, I'm sorry — missing cartons are the worst kind of problem because you can't absorb it; someone downstream is waiting.

Here's how I'll find it. The freight station keeps a tally of every carton when the container is devanned, and the loading list from origin tells us what went in. Comparing those two says whether it was short-shipped or lost on the last leg. The delivery receipt fills the gaps.

Can you send me your count by carton and model, with photos of what arrived? That goes next to their numbers, not instead.

I'll have the comparison by {{next_update_time}}, and if it points to the depot I'll be on them that day. If it points to origin, your supplier hears from me, not from you.

Hi {{customer_name}} — on the missing cartons, here's the plan.

I'm pulling three records: origin loading list, the freight station tally, and the delivery receipt. Where they disagree tells us if this was short-shipped or lost after devanning.

scripts.use_when: 客户第一次被告知 CFIA 或 Health Canada 要求补件；先问清被扣类别，只讲命中项
scripts.text:
Hi {{customer_name}}, I know this feels like a rule appearing out of nowhere. It isn't new, but that doesn't help you today — so let's work out which requirement actually applies.

What I've confirmed: the shipment is held because the goods fall under CFIA or Health Canada requirements, and the requirement depends on what's in the cartons. Tell me which line is held — food, cosmetics, a medical device or the wood packaging — and I'll confirm only that requirement, not a list of all four.

I'm pulling the exact rule from the CFIA import reference system today, plus a written list of what's missing for your category.

I'll message you every day at the same time until this closes, including days with no change. If something breaks in between, you hear it from me first.
